premises.text: People are hardwired to respond to immediate rewards, making them prone to impulse spending.
premises.evidence_span: our brain was designed 50,000 years ago to be good at one thing, hunting and gathering.

premises.text: Current personal finance products fail to help people save effectively.
premises.evidence_span: all the products in the landscape today in personal finance are coming from the same vantage point that in order to do well with your finances, you must create a plan, you must have a budget, you must stick to that financial diet.

premises.text: Impulse Save allows users to save money instantly when they choose not to make an impulse purchase.
premises.evidence_span: as an impulse save user, Ann has options she didn't have before.

premises.text: Users can create savings goals that motivate them to save.
premises.evidence_span: they create goals. And a goal can be anything from an iPad, to a travel vacation, to paying down your student debt.

premises.text: Impulse Save provides notifications and updates to encourage saving behavior.
premises.evidence_span: we do that through email updates and progress updates. We do that through notifications.

premises.text: Users can save money through various platforms, including social media and SMS.
premises.evidence_span: you can impulse save using Instagram. Just use the impulse save hashtag.

value.text: Users can save money easily and effectively through Impulse Save.
value.evidence_span: our savers are saving over $3,000 a year right now.

notes: No separate premises for user sharing and social aspects as they support the main premise of saving behavior.
